title: Streaming and Suspense
description: Learn how React Suspense and Next.js streaming send HTML progressively to the browser, improving perceived performance and user experience.

data.text: Streaming is a technique where the server sends parts of the page to the browser as soon as they are ready, instead of waiting for the entire page to finish rendering. Combined with React Suspense, streaming lets users see and interact with content while slower parts of the page are still loading.

In Next.js, streaming is automatic when you use Suspense boundaries around Server Components. The browser receives the static parts of the page immediately and fills in the slower sections with placeholders until the data is ready.

In traditional server rendering, the server waits for every data request to finish before sending any HTML. Streaming changes this: the server sends a shell of the page immediately and streams in remaining chunks as they complete. Users see the layout faster and can start interacting sooner.

items: The browser receives the page layout and static content first
Slow data fetches happen in the background on the server
Completed sections are streamed to the browser as HTML chunks
Users see meaningful content sooner, even on slow networks

data.text: Suspense is a React feature that lets you display a fallback while a part of the UI is loading. In Next.js, wrap slow Server Components in a Suspense boundary. The boundary shows a loading state until the component finishes fetching and rendering on the server.

data.title: Suspense boundaries around slow components
data.content: Wrapping slow Server Components in Suspense boundaries so each section streams independently.
data.code:
import { Suspense } from 'react' import { Recommendations } from './Recommendations' import { Reviews } from './Reviews' async function ProductPage({ id }: { id: string }) { const product = await fetchProduct(id) return (

{product.name}

{product.description}

Loading recommendations...

}> Loading reviews...

}>
) }

data.text: Next.js automatically wraps a route segment in a Suspense boundary when you create a loading.tsx file. The framework shows the loading UI while the Server Components in that segment finish loading data. This is the easiest way to add streaming without writing explicit Suspense boundaries.

data.title: Loading file with skeleton UI
data.content: A loading.tsx file with skeleton loaders that display while the page segment loads.

data.text: Streaming works best when combined with progressive enhancement. Build the page so the most important content appears first, then progressively load secondary content like recommendations, related items, or comments. Users on fast connections may not notice streaming at all, but users on slow networks get a much better experience.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Place Suspense boundaries around slow, non-critical components. Critical content like the main article or product details should load normally without a boundary so it appears immediately.

data.title: Summary
points: Streaming sends parts of the page to the browser as soon as they are ready.
React Suspense boundaries define which sections can stream independently.
Next.js loading.tsx files automatically create these boundaries.
The result is faster perceived performance and a smoother experience on slow networks.
